subject: Rapid surge & transient throttle in reserved GPU pool — recovery plan and scheduled verification
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@clearsight.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Rapid surge & transient throttle in reserved GPU pool — initial incident note

Hi Olivia,

Wanted to send a concise note while we're actively working the tail-end of the event. This morning (UTC 16:05) your dedicated GPU pool in us-west experienced a rapid throughput surge that triggered autoscaler backpressure and temporary request throttling across a subset of nodes. The customer-visible effect was elevated latency and a small number of aborted requests for ~18 minutes.

What we know so far:
- Root trigger: sudden concentrated burst of concurrent token generation from a single service in your account; sequence lengths were higher than your baseline workload.
- Observable behavior: autoscaler delayed warm-up for 3 out of 6 newly provisioned nodes due to a timing race in the warmup path; requests routed to nodes with smaller active cache led to increased per-token latency and in a few cases early terminations.
- Immediate remediation: we raised short-term headroom (warm spare nodes), disabled the aggressive affinity that was contributing to hot-spotting, and applied a temporary autoscaler tuning profile.

Next steps I'm proposing:
1) We will run a joint canary test (Redwood + ClearSight) to reproduce the workload shape and validate autoscaler warmup under controlled surge traffic.
2) We'll share evidence artifacts and a short technical appendix describing the timing race and mitigations.
3) We will offer a goodwill credit (details below) and schedule a 60-minute technical review.

Proposed dates for the canary: Aug 3 or Aug 4 — low-traffic window you pick. Please confirm which works.

I've looped in Marissa (ops) and Ben (billing) for runbook and credit logistics.

Attachment: we'll upload raw traces + allocator snapshots to a shared Drive folder and link in a follow-up.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll get this fully validated and locked down.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

[Attachment stub: pool-throttle-evidence.tar.gz (1.2MB)]

From: Olivia Park <olivia@clearsight.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Sweeney <mark@clearsight.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rapid surge & transient throttle in reserved GPU pool — initial incident note

Thanks for the quick update, Nikhil.

We saw elevated tail latency in our dashboards and a handful of user-facing errors during the window you described. Appreciate the immediate headroom. A couple of asks before we lock in a test date:
- Please share the allocator snapshots and any tracing that ties the aborted requests to node warmup.
- Can you confirm the exact credit amount and how it will be applied to our invoice?
- Aug 4 is preferable for the canary for us (we have low traffic that day).

If you have a short checklist for what we need to enable on our side (headers, synthetic payload shape), send it over and we'll get engineering aligned.

Olivia Park
Director of Engineering, ClearSight Labs
olivia@clearsight.ai

[Inline: ops@clearsight.ai will monitor during the test]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@clearsight.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rapid surge & transient throttle in reserved GPU pool — artifacts, credit, and canary plan

Olivia / Mark —

Thanks for the preference on Aug 4. Per your asks: attaching the technical appendix and a canary plan (PDF) that outlines the exact traffic shape, headers, and sequence-length distributions to use. The Drive folder contains: allocator snapshots, trace spans, and node logs. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-canary-evidence

Credit: Ben is proposing a one-time invoice credit equal to 6 hours of reserved capacity at your committed rate (applies to invoice CS-8943). Ben — please confirm and I'll pass to Olivia.

Short checklist for ClearSight test-side:
- Ramp target concurrency from 0 -> 60 over 90s, with a 95th-percentile sequence length similar to your peak profile (see appendix section 2).
- Include the header X-Request-Flow: clearsight-canary and use the test API key we'll provision in the shared secret.
- Maintain a background traffic baseline at ~10% of normal production to ensure warm caches vary across nodes.

Ops runbook highlights we'll execute on our side:
- Validate autoscaler warm-spare inventory and confirm the warmup window metrics (KV cache hits, model init time).
- Watch for allocator thrash and, if observed, temporarily route burst traffic to dedicated warm pool.
- Collect full CPU/GPU telemetry and per-request trace spans to the Drive folder.

Attachments included: autoscaler-canary-plan.pdf, runbook-checklist.md, pool-throttle-evidence.tar.gz.

Best,
Nikhil

[Attachment stubs: autoscaler-canary-plan.pdf, runbook-checklist.md]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-03T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rapid surge & transient throttle in reserved GPU pool — ops plan

Nikhil / team —

Quick ops confirmations ahead of Aug 4 test:
- Canary environment will run in us-west-2 isolated lane to avoid cross-tenant bleed.
- We'll provision two warm spare nodes (p4d-sim) for the window and enable extra telemetry sampling.
- If we observe >30% queue growth for more than 2 consecutive minutes we'll enable immediate spillover to the warm pool (manual override).

Checklist summary (short):
- 07:45 UTC: infra smoke check & secret exchange.
- 08:00 UTC: start baseline synthetic at 10%.
- 08:30 UTC: ramp test per plan.
- 09:15 UTC: hold & validate artifacts.

I'll be on the call to handle node-level rollbacks. Ben — PTL on credits, please confirm the invoice action.

-Marissa
Senior Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

[One-line addendum: we'll also run a short negative test (slightly higher sequence length) to ensure graceful degradation behavior is unchanged.]

We also appreciate the clarity on the ops checklist; we'll generate the synthetic payload as described and share our small test harness repo link shortly.

Looking forward to validating this together.

Olivia Park
Director of Engineering, ClearSight Labs
